title: MLOps Partner Integration Battlecard (draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight battlecard for commercial / SE teams to use when engaging MLOps platform partners (CI/CD, data pipelines, model registries, feature stores). Goal: enable fast qualification, surface integration win themes, and hand off a clear technical pilot checklist to partner engineering and the customer's platform team.

Primary audience
- Solutions Engineers (first 15–30 minutes qualification)
- Partner/Alliance reps during joint calls
- Account execs prepping for procurement-level conversations

Elevator pitch (1–2 lines)
Redwood Inference provides a unified, production-ready inference runtime that slides into an MLOps partner workflow with minimal changes: we serve model variants at predictable latency & cost while handing back observability and rollout controls to the partner's CI/CD and registry.

Top 6 partner-value themes to call out
1) Easy endpoint alignment: use model version tags from partner registries — no rewrites to existing CI flow.
2) Predictable economics: reserved capacity + autoscale policies map to partner cost-allocation models.
3) Security-first: VPC tunneling, KMS support, and audit logs fit compliance stacks.
4) Observability handoff: token-level cost & latency metrics can be piped into partner dashboards.
5) Graceful fallbacks: routing policies allow partner orchestration to prefer cheaper/quantized variants under load.
6) Pilot speed: 48–72 hour proof-of-concept for a single route using snapshot models and canned data.

Qualify in the first 10 minutes (quick checklist questions)
- Which model registry do you use? (MLflow, S3 tags, Hugging Face, internal)
- How do you currently version and pin models in pipelines? (semantic tags, commit hash, stage)
- Is inference currently inside the same VPC as model training or separate?
- Do you have hard latency budgets per route (p50/p95)? What are they?
- How is cost charged back? e.g., per team, per project, or shared infra?
- Do you need private deployment (VPC/on-prem) or hosted API for the pilot?

Common technical objections + quick responses
Objection: "We already have an inference runtime."
- Response: "Great — many partners keep their heavy training/CI in-house and use Redwood as the production serving tier to manage elasticity, observability and fallback economics. We can run side-by-side as a migration path; no rip-and-replace required."

Objection: "Integration will break our CI pipelines."
- Response: "We support standard registry hooks and a simple adapter for model artifacts. Typical integration adds a 1–2 step deploy job to call Redwood's model pin API; we provide example GitHub Actions and Jenkins snippets."

Objection: "We can't expose data or keys to a hosted third party."
- Response: "We have Private (VPC/on‑prem) options, HSM/KMS integrations, and provide a security workbook for SOC2/ISO evidence. For pilots we can run in a customer VPC with ephemeral creds."

Quick technical pilot plan (48–72h minimal scope)
1) Pre-call prep (SE + partner engineer): confirm model artifact location, example input/output, target route latency (p95) and SLO.
2) Day 0: deploy a pinned model variant (quantized small if needed) to Redwood sandbox; run 100 synthetic requests — capture latency/cost metrics.
3) Day 1: swap in real sample dataset (anonymized), run load test to p95 target, validate KV cache priming.
4) Day 2: integrate partner's rollout hook: simulate a canary traffic shift and validate fallback to a cheaper variant.
5) Exit criteria: logged traces in partner dashboard + Redwood console, documented p95 under target, cost per 1k tokens within +/-20% of projection.

Integration checklist (for partner eng handoff)
- Model artifact access: URI and auth method
- Versioning convention (tag -> Redwood model pin mapping)
- Network shape: public, VPC peering, or private link
- Secrets management: KMS/HSM or temporary API keys
- Observability endpoints to forward metrics/traces
- Rollout triggers: webhook contract for canary/rollback

SE play snippets (copy/paste)
Email to partner engineering: 
"Hi <name>,
We can run a 48–72h pilot to validate latency and rollout. Can you share an example model artifact URI, a sample input file (100 rows), and your registry tag pattern? We'll provision a sandbox model pin and share a short runbook for the deploy. Typical outcome: p95 latency, traceable calls in your observability, and a documented cost estimate for 1M tokens.
Best,
Ava (Redwood SE)"

Demo checklist (for joint calls)
- Show registry -> Redwood pin workflow end-to-end (screen share)
- Run a live small-batch inference (streamed output)
- Flip traffic to a quantized variant; show latency and cost delta in console
- Show canary rollback triggered via webhook
- Open partner dashboard and show metric forwarding

Go-to-market motions / co-sell hooks
- Co-branded pilot collateral (one-pager) for joint prospects
- Partner engineering office hours during pilot week (2x 1-hr slots)
- Joint webinar: "From model registry to production: 1-week path" (90-min)
- Referral credits for partner-sourced pilots that convert to Dedicated contracts

Commercial signals to watch (deal qualification)
- Prospect already committed to a model registry + CI/CD workflows
- Prospect budgets for cloud infra or reserved capacity in next 60–90 days
- Platform/infra team involvement indicated (not just product team)

Risk areas & mitigations
- Data security concerns: offer Private deployment plan + security workbook
- Unexpected latency during holidays: set conservative SLOs, enable autoscale headroom
- Billing surprise: provide upfront 30-day cost projection using sample token counts and recommend reserved capacity option

Open questions for product/eng (internal notes)
- Need a concise GitHub Actions example repo specifically for MLflow -> Redwood pin (ticket ENG-1428).
- Can we surface sample `cost-per-1k-tokens` quick calculator in the SE console?
- Confirm which observability tags map back to partner trace IDs by default.

Attachments / quick links
- GitHub adapter PR: github:repo/redwood-mlops-adapter/pull/27
- Confluence checklist: confluence:ML-Partner-Framework-2025
- Pilot tracking board: JIRA board (linked in intake form)

Notes to self (informal)
- Try this at partner summit 2026 runbook session.
- Shorten demo script to 5 mins for exec-level calls; focus on "flip to quantized variant" as the wow moment.

End of draft
